features.headline: Inside the evolution of Caleb Williams' MVP candidacy
features.desc: Williams has the fourth-shortest odds to win MVP as the Bears are currently favored to win the NFC.
body: Chicago Bears wide receiver Luther Burden III ran back to the visitors sideline at Seattle's Lumen Field on Monday night with a message for quarterback Caleb Williams.

The Bears had just accomplished a rare feat. Before Burden caught a 1-yard touchdown pass at the end of an opening drive that spanned 8 minutes, 32 seconds, the last team to score a touchdown against Seattle on its first possession was the 49ers in Week 1 of the 2025 season.
"I went up to him and told him I don't care who they is," the wide receiver said about the defending Super Bowl champs. "No. 1 defense, I don't care."
After slapping hands with his teammate, Williams stood up from the bench and echoed Burden's sentiment.
"I don't give a f—- who they are!" Williams yelled.

Chicago's 34-17 takedown of the Seahawks capped a unique set of primetime performances as the Bears beat Super Bowl runner-up New England in Week 7 and the defending champs in back-to-back games. It was the first such sequence in franchise history.

The victory made the Bears the favorites to represent the NFC in Super Bowl LXI, and it planted Williams firmly in the MVP conversation. Williams entered Week 9 with the fourth-shortest odds (+500) to win MVP, according to DraftKings Sportsbook.
He trailed the Buffalo Bills' Josh Allen (+165), San Francisco 49ers' Brock Purdy (+450) and Cincinnati Bengals' Joe Burrow (+475).

The Bears (6-2) have won all three games since Williams returned from a hamstring injury that sidelined him Weeks 3-5. In fact, they haven't trailed in any of the three and have topped 30 points each time.

features.headline: Bengals face Falcons S Jessie Bates III, evoking mixed emotions
features.desc: Cincinnati hasn't been to the playoffs since Bates' departure, but Atlanta also hasn't reached the postseason since his arrival.
body: MADRID — When the Cincinnati Bengals step on the field at the Santiago Bernabeu in Madrid on Sunday to face the Atlanta Falcons, the Bengals will be posed with a question it once forced other teams to ask.
How does one account for safety Jessie Bates III?
From 2018 to 2022, Bates emerged as one of Cincinnati's best playmakers in the team's run to the Super Bowl at the end of the 2021 season.
But after Bates left Cincinnati in free agency, he has spent the past four seasons with the Falcons, with whom he has maintained his perch as one of the best in the NFL.
And ahead of Sunday's game, Bates was asked how much he thinks about the events that led him to leave the team that drafted him.

"Coming here to Atlanta has changed my life, my family's trajectory, what that looks like moving forward," Bates told ESPN. "But at the same time, it's like, damn, you want to play in meaningful football games.
I haven't played in the playoffs since I left there. And I don't think they've been in the playoffs, either, since I left."
Bates is correct. The Falcons (3-5) could use a win to jump-start their season and break a nine-year postseason drought. Cincinnati (5-2) is looking to secure its first playoff berth since 2022.

That was Bates' last season with Cincinnati, which drafted him in 2018 with a second-round pick. Bengals coach Zac Taylor, who arrived a year after Bates was drafted, recalled how the former Wake Forest standout went from a young player adjusting to a new scheme to an ascending star.

features.headline: Joe Burrow makes time for art in Madrid ahead of Bengals-Falcons
features.desc: While in Spain, the Bengals quarterback is finding time for one of his off-field interests: art.
body: MADRID — Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow knows what he wants to do with his free time exploring Madrid ahead of Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons. Forget football — well, at least the American kind.

The Cincinnati star, who attracted a massive media gathering Friday, said that if he gets a chance to wind down, he'd like to indulge one of his many off-field interests and see the art around the Spanish capital.
"I'd like to go see some more museums and go to an art gallery and do a little shopping, but we'll see," Burrow said.

The Pro Bowler and two-time MVP finalist already accomplished some of that earlier in the week when he stopped by the Museo del Prado during Cincinnati's first off day in Madrid. The team arrived from Cincinnati on Wednesday morning, which allowed him some time to go explore.

And even if he wasn't back home, it doesn't mean he didn't go unnoticed. He said he ran into a group of students from the United States who are studying abroad who recognized him. It's fitting for a person whose profile has grown well beyond the game in recent years.

"It's often a little more than I expect when I'm in a different country," Burrow said. "I usually expect to go pretty incognito and not have anybody recognize me. It's usually a little more than that. But I love being out here because I can feel like a normal person for a little bit."

Burrow and the Bengals (5-2) have spent the week trying to balance being tourists and also preparing for a showdown against the Falcons (3-5) at the historic Santiago Bernabeu stadium, which is home to Real Madrid.

features.headline: What Yankees, Mets can do this winter to meet their 2027 goals
features.desc: The 2026 MLB season didn't go as either New York team planned. Here's how they can flip the script next year.
body: With a lockout looming on Dec. 1, the consensus across Major League Baseball is that November will be a frenetic month, similar to the lead-up to the 2021 lockout. Free agents will come off the board. Trades will be made. There will be a flurry of player movement before the league shuts down.

The action, according to sources, is expected to start as soon as next week, when the industry convenes at the general managers meetings in Las Vegas. And you can expect the two New York clubs will be involved.

The Yankees and Mets experienced very different versions of disappointment in 2026. The Yankees reached the postseason for the eighth time in nine years under manager Aaron Boone, only to get bounced by an American League East rival in the division series for the second straight year.
The Mets, meanwhile, did not make the playoffs for the second consecutive season, finishing last in the National League East despite having one of baseball's two most expensive payrolls.

Both teams will dabble in the free agent and trade markets to bolster their rosters this offseason. Here are three needs we believe each team will address to get over the hump by the time Opening Day comes around — whenever that is.
1. Rebuild the bullpen (starting with closer David Bednar?)

Pitching was not the problem for the Yankees in 2026. They led the majors in staff ERA by a good margin. But while they have a surplus of starters, they'll need to fill out their bullpen again this offseason.
As it stands, left-hander Brent Headrick is the only reliever under team control for next season who had at least 17 appearances in 2026.
